chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, said:

I wrote to al-'Abd al-Salih عليه السلام: A man prays on a cloudy day in an open land, and he does not know the qiblah, so he prays. Then, when he finishes his salat, the sun appears to him, and he realizes that he had prayed toward other than the qiblah. Should his salat be counted, or should he repeat it? So he wrote: He should repeat it so long as the time has not passed him.
Does he not know that Allah, Exalted is He, says—and His word is the truth—: “So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah.”

key_terms.الْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ: a title referring to the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الْوَقْتُ: the prescribed time of the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer) that is being evaluated for validity
key_terms.فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا: wherever you turn; a Qur'anic phrase about direction
key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: the Face of Allah; Qur'anic expression in the cited verse
key_terms.يُعِيدُهَا: he repeats it, meaning he performs the prayer again

ai.seo_question: If someone unknowingly prays in the wrong qiblah direction, must the salat be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who prays in the wrong direction due to uncertainty about the qiblah on a cloudy day. The Imam عليه السلام states that the prayer must be repeated if the prayer time still remains, while invoking the Qur'anic verse about turning wherever one may turn as part of the discussion.
